study_identification_part.si4_title: Transdiagnostic dimensions of psychopathology explain individuals' unique deviations from normative neurodevelopment in brain structure

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction explicitly state that the study builds normative models of cortical volume in healthy individuals and tests whether deviation-based scores better predict dimensions of psychopathology than raw cortical volume. They also compare deviation-based predictions to raw features and examine transdiagnostic and case–control effects.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "...we built normative models of cortical volume and tested whether deviations from these models better predicted psychiatric symptoms compared to raw cortical volume."; "...we performed conventional case–control comparisons..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: Healthy controls were defined as individuals with no clinically significant symptoms. They split 1,271 participants into healthy vs. psychopathology; 281 healthy controls were used to train the normative model. Imaging quality standards and exclusion reasons (radiological abnormalities, QA failures, corrupted data, missing demographics, familial relations) are described, with counts leading to the final sample size.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "A total of 381 individuals reported no clinically significant symptoms... The remaining 281 healthy individuals were designated as our normative training subset."; "...160 were excluded due to gross radiological abnormalities... 47 ... did not pass rigorous ... quality assurance; one ... corrupted data... 17 ... missing demographic data... 105 ... shared a familial link... This process left a final sample of 1,271 participants."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative model predicted regional cortical volume from age and sex. The dataset was single-site/single-scanner, so no multi-site harmonization was needed. They further note clear effects of sex and age and controlled them in prediction analyses.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "...we used gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict cortical volume values from age and sex..."; "All scanning was done using the same sequences on the same scanner..."; "As we often observed clear effects of age and sex, we controlled age and sex in our prediction models."
